title: Station keeping: stop the drift
summary: Your geostationary satellite is slowly drifting away from its assigned longitude.
goals: Understand why a GEO satellite drifts in longitude
Plan and execute a small east-west manoeuvre
situation: The orbit is about 2 km higher than geostationary, so the satellite is slightly slower than the Earth's rotation and drifts west. Stop the drift with a small retrograde burn on the reaction-control thrusters.

steps.text: Read the drift in the Orbit group (about -0.025 deg/day).
Burn RETROGRADE about 0.07 m/s: prop.rea BURN RETROGRADE 0.073
steps.hint: Change in orbit radius: da = 2 a dv / v. Lowering the orbit 2 km needs ~0.073 m/s.
If you overshot, burn PROGRADE a little.

successText: Station kept. Real GEO satellites do this every couple of weeks, plus north-south burns for inclination.
